title: Using the registers of the clarinet in solos
summary: Simeon covers the whole instrument, often moving from low to middle to upper register by the last chorus, like Noone.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Yeah. I remember some people have discussed, like Johnny Dodge used to sometimes stick to one register, play a whole solo in a low register. Maybe in the next chorus he'd play it in the upper register. Well, they say like noon, and I notice you do the same way, because you cover the whole instrument all over.
Yeah, in all registers, yeah. And usually on the last chorus then you, in your upper register then, your higher notes.

Did you ever try that style, just sticking to the low register for one chorus? Do you, I haven't heard you so much in recent years, to tell you the truth, I heard you last winter in New York, it's the last I've heard you.
On some solos I play in the lower register.

Play maybe one course in the lower register then, it depends on the amount of choruses that you're playing. You're playing two choruses or three choruses, then I usually play a chorus in the lower register, maybe one in the middle register and the last one in the upper register, when you reach the climax. But I very seldom play in one register. Usually I cover the whole instrument, you know. I like the letter T, T-U-T-U.
